column1: # The do-unit registry-replay class (found by the variation sweep,
# 2026-07-13; fixed to a SOUND REFUSAL the same day). Was: a compiled
# `do [...]` body containing a registry-mutating statement replayed it
# against the check pass's surviving state (typed defs raised a
# type-conflict Error; check-time registrations were invisible). Now: the
# bake decision refuses a body carrying a capitalised def
# (eng bodyHasReplayHazard) so the interpreter owns these rows with full
# parity, and the import half compiles natively as a closure unit after the
# ensureExportsBound namespace re-bind fix. Value defs (`do [def b 5 …]`)
# were never affected. Full graduation = the Phase 6 JIT detached-unit
# cache compiles these bodies as units, at which point the rows compile
# natively and their ledger entries delete.
# GRADUATED 2026-07-14 (do-def leak fidelity): both typed-def rows compile
# natively as closure units and moved to lang/spec/bytecode-migrated.tsv.
# ── Added 2026-08-28 and REMOVED the same day; the note stays because the
#    round trip is the finding. stampFnConst's container descent stamps the
#    fn values inside a map const, which made these two mount-handler seeds
#    refuse: compileStoredFnUnit analyses against the LIVE emit state, so the
#    ENCLOSING compile inherited a dynamic-scope promotion decision and a dep
#    record from a body it may never apply. Two rows landed here as ledgered
#    refusals.
#    The justification for ledgering them was that without the descent the
#    `for`-wrapped seed MISCOMPILES (a flex map captured by a mount handler
#    loses its identity across loop iterations: the compiled run raises
#    `expected a FlexMap, got FlexMap` where the interpreter round-trips),
#    and a refusal beats a wrong answer. That justification was the mistake.
#    The descent was not FIXING that miscompile, it was MASKING it — the
#    stamp is an optimisation that declines for a capturing fn, for a body
#    whose lowering refuses, and whenever runtime stamping is unarmed, so the
#    wrong answer would have come back silently the first time any of those
#    held.
#    The stamp now restores es.dynScopeNames and declines rather than perturb
#    the enclosing program, and an optional ref no longer escalates a rebind
#    to a program-level refusal. Both rows compile again, both buckets are
#    gone, and the flex-map divergence is pinned honestly where divergences
#    belong — varyKnownMiscompiles in test/go/langspec/vary_differential_test.go.
